idiom_name: functools.singledispatch with one registration per element type
implementation_notes: Python needs no interface set and no accept method: a single-dispatch generic function registers one implementation per element type, an element with no registration falls back to the base implementation, and registrations can live in the module next to the element they handle - which is the acyclic property expressed directly in the language. What replaces the classic accept/visit structure is functools.singledispatch plus the register attribute, with the base implementation deciding the failure mode (raise NotImplementedError to be loud, or do the generic case to stay open). Keep a hand-written accept when the operation must reach private element state or when a visitor has to be substituted per instance, since singledispatch keys on the runtime type of the first argument only.
pitfalls: Dispatch looks only at the type of the first argument, so an operation that varies with a second argument cannot be expressed and silently ignores it.
The fallback defines the failure mode: raising is loud and safe, while an object-level default quietly absorbs every newly added element type and hides the missing implementation.
Registrations can be added from anywhere, so two modules registering the same type make the winner depend on import order; keep one registration per type and assert on duplicates in tests.
